subject: System Design
title: Tables, Rows, and Schemas
description: A short lesson to help you apply Tables, Rows, and Schemas.

hook.text: A relational database organizes data into tables with rows and columns — like a spreadsheet with strict rules.

buildup.text: Each table has a schema defining column names, data types, and constraints like NOT NULL or UNIQUE.

discovery.text: The schema enforces data integrity: you can't store a string in an integer column or leave a required field empty.

twist.text: Schema changes on large tables can lock the database for hours. Evolving schemas at scale is a real challenge.

climax.text: Relational schemas trade flexibility for correctness. Every row in a table follows the same structure.

punchline.text: Strict schemas prevent bad data from entering the system.

quiz.question: What does a database schema enforce?
options: Data types, constraints, and structure for every row
